## Findings
- claim-1: For \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), the two proposed families are \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6@L14-L33|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: For \((r,q,i,j)=(5,3,2,2)\), \(a=1,b=2,N=\binom31=3\), and the two families are \(F_1=(22,32,33)\) and \(F_2=(22,221,222)\). [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]
- claim-3: In the \(3^5\)-box, the Schur-span module for shapes containing \(22\) has \(40\) ordered Schur columns. For \(F_1\), the complementary-column order is \[ \begin{gathered} 221;2211,222,321;22111,2221,3211,322,331;\\ 22211,2222,32111,3221,3311,332; 22221,32211,3222,33111,3321,333;\\ 22222,32221,33211,3322,3331; 32222,33221,33311,3332; 33222,33321,3333;33322,33331;33332;33333 . \end{gathered} \] The selected Pieri rows in the retained artifact order give a \(37\times37\) complementary minor of absolute determinant \(1\). [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]
- claim-4: The separately formed direct-LR relation rows reduce integrally to the selected Pieri rows: the artifact retains, for each LR row, its integer coefficient vector in the fixed selected-row order. Hence the LR and selected-Pieri relation lattices agree for both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\). [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]
- claim-5: The resulting Smith quotients are torsion-free of rank \(3\): \[ J_{v_{5,5,4,8}}/\Lambda_+J_{v_{5,5,4,8}}\cong\mathbb Z^3, \] with respective bases given by the images of \(F_1\) and \(F_2\), subject to the standard integral box-model identification of this quotient. [artifact e03b87dfaac58fc8c68b65e28c061cd1ac2d9a04b2e72c5e80e07ffd2ad7d00f]
## Strategy
Use the retained artifact only provisionally for \((r,q,i,j)=(5,3,2,2)\), hence \(v_{5,5,4,8}\), with \(a=1,b=2,N=3\) and
\[
F_1=(22,32,33),\qquad F_2=(22,221,222).
\]
For each family, require a fixed full column order, selected-Pieri-row order, a displayed \(37\times37\) complementary minor of determinant \(\pm1\), and integral reductions of every Pieri and direct-LR row into the selected Pieri lattice. Explicitly match each selected Pieri row \(h_k s_\mu\) to its LR row with \(\alpha=(k)\), proving reverse containment.

Deduce the Smith type from the unimodular complementary minor and all-Pieri containment, rather than describing it as independently Smith-computed. Under the box-model and Schur-span hypotheses, this gives the conditional quotient \(\mathbb Z^3\); graded Nakayama then yields conditional irredundance of both prescribed families.

## Gaps
- The immutable computed claims remain unsupported; their artifact contents are not displayed here.
- The critic identifies missing inspectable row orders, the \(F_2\) minor certificate, explicit all-Pieri reductions, and selected-Pieri/direct-LR matching.
- The two constructions have shared combinatorial and linear-algebra infrastructure, so they are not fully independent implementations.
- No separate Smith-normal-form implementation or independent replay/audit of retained reduction vectors is supplied.
- The conclusion depends on the standard integral box-model, the identification of \(J_v\) with the indicated Schur-span ideal, and generation by each family.

## Next
- Retain a complete certificate for both \(F_1\) and \(F_2\): orders, selected rows, determinants, and integral coefficient vectors for all Pieri and LR reductions.
- Add exact selected-Pieri \(=\) LR-\((k)\) row comparisons.
- Obtain an independently implemented LR/Smith audit, or leave Smith form as a deduction from the unimodular lattice certificate.
- Keep minimality explicitly conditional until these finite certificates and hypotheses are independently checked.
